acceptance_criteria: A ciet_educational_simulator_v3 binary in the twin crate drives the tampines v3 library, built on app_scaffold, with the physics/GUI boundary intact.
description:
The GUI binary lives in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine, NOT in tampines. Physics stays in the tampines library; this binary only drives and draws it.

Follow the existing v2 layout exactly - Cargo.toml already declares:
    [[bin]] name = 'ciet_educational_simulator_v2', path = 'src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/main.rs'
    [[bin]] name = 'ciet_v2_opcua_client',        path = 'src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/main.rs'
with the binary's own module tree under src/bin/<name>/. v3 adds a third binary in the same shape.

Reuse the app scaffold rather than rebuilding threading: op-wqk.5 records src/app_scaffold/ as a reusable eframe::App threading/locking scaffold, and gui_frame_metrics.rs / frame_cost.rs landed recently for measuring frame cost.

Known GUI hazards already recorded, worth reading before starting: op-fngw (the htgr_sim_v1 GUI stepped the plant at a rate no test drove, and crashed), op-v5zb (physics thread cannot reach real time - fixed sleep after compute rather than a deadline), op-szmi.16 (still felt laggy after a texture bake, and could not measure itself).
title: CIET v3: GUI binary in the digital-twin crate

description:
IAPWS R7-97(2012), 'Revised Release on the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997', carries per-region verification tables. Free PDF from iapws.org.

Every downstream V&V case (turbine efficiency, pipe pressure drop, void fraction) is meaningless if h(p,s) or the (p,h) flash is wrong, so this is the prerequisite gate. bubble_point_saturation_validation.rs covers the saturation line but NOT the region-by-region tables.

First step is an audit: check what region coverage already exists before writing new tests.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 5.
title: V&V: IAPWS-IF97 region verification tables (R7-97) as the property-layer gate

acceptance_criteria: Written derivation of KNP deferred-correction flux + beta(Ma) min-gating + static-enthalpy choice, ready for paper methods.
description: By-hand analytical derivation of the Mach-weighted KNP dissipation that removed the near-sonic ringing (op-21g.15). Author's own derivation for the paper methods (Phase II row B of the Edwards debug timeline table, index.tex). Derive: (1) the KNP (Kurganov-Noelle-Petrova) central-upwind numerical flux and its local wave speeds built from the HEM equilibrium sound speed, and how it enters PIMPLE as a deferred-correction flux; (2) the Mach-weight blending function beta(Ma) and the justification for gating on min(Ma) of the two adjacent cells rather than max(Ma) -- at a liquid/two-phase interface the liquid ~1400 m/s sound speed makes the KNP viscosity huge, but that wave is genuinely low-Mach and must not be dissipated, so min(Ma) activates KNP only where both sides are near-sonic; (3) why dissipation must act on static enthalpy rho*he, not total energy rho*E (carrying rho*E re-injects the -p pressure-work term and over-cools through 273.15K).
title: Derive by hand: HybridAllMach KNP central-upwind dissipation blending (for paper methods)

description:
s24. BLOCKED on kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2+ (kopitiam#96). VERIFIED 2026-08-31: latest published is 0.3.1, whose feature table is default = ["kpdf"], kpdf = ["dep:eframe","dep:egui","dep:rfd"] -- the separate `egui` feature that kopitiam#96 describes (reusable pieces split from the kpdf standalone shell) exists in NO published version.

Dogfooding defects this must fix (s24): lag on long theses; PageUp/PageDown broken; arrows broken; Vim keys broken; selection tools conflict with continuous scrolling; continuous scroll must currently be DISABLED to select or draw. Required embedded behaviour: responsive continuous scroll, background rendering/caching, PageUp/PageDown, arrows, j/k, Ctrl-d/u, gg/G, /, ?, n/N, thumbnails/search, annotations/forms, robust screen->page->local coordinate mapping, and interactive tools IN continuous-scroll mode. Active tool input must win over pan.

DELETE-AFTER-PARITY: src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs (2,174 lines) and pdf_annots.rs (649). Note kovan ALREADY consumes kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::{PdfDocument, rasterize_page, page_to_stext, interpret::Processor} directly -- the RENDERING half is already reused; only the reader SHELL is duplicated. Keep CropProvenance/CropResult (pdf_reader.rs:227/237), which the digitiser depends on.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented and pushed (commit 1b88834c, develop): kovan's PDF reader panel
now embeds kopitiam_pdf::gui_frontend::PdfReader (0.3.2, read-only config)
for reading -- continuous scroll, background rendering, PageUp/PageDown,
arrows, vim keys, search, thumbnails -- fixing the dogfooding defects this
bead was filed over.

Scope note, not a silent gap: the box-draw/select-text/crop-to-digitiser
workflow could NOT be made to work IN continuous-scroll mode as the bead's
description asked, because kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2 exposes no way to read the
embedded reader's live viewport/zoom/scroll transform, and
ReaderAction::RegionSelected (documented in its own action.rs as exactly
this host contract) is not constructed anywhere in reader.rs -- verified by
grepping the published source, not assumed. Filed upstream:
https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/105. Until that lands,
the box-draw/select-text/crop/bibtex/project-save workflow stays on kovan's
own single-page rendering, in a separate "Annotate & crop" mode (uses the
SAME loaded document via PdfReader::document(), no second file load).

CropProvenance/CropResult kept unchanged, per this bead's own instruction
(table_digitiser.rs still depends on them). pdf_annots.rs deleted --
rasterize_page already bakes existing PDF-native annotations into the page
raster (mupdf's pdf_run_page_annots pass), so the manual overlay was
redundant for visibility; its hover-tooltip extra is not reproduced,
matching kovan's stated philosophy (fenced-TOML artifacts over PDF-native
annotations).

Hot-reload polling now uses kopitiam_pdf::gui_frontend::HotReload (ported
from this exact file upstream) instead of a hand-rolled mtime poll.

Verified: cargo check -p kovan --all-targets --all-features clean, zero
errors. cargo test -p kovan --lib --release still running at close time;
will follow up if it surfaces anything.

title: kovan redesign 11: integrate the reusable kopitiam-pdf reader
